text: Woven in Cairo in 1910. We still have the workshop's receipt, with the stamp. That is rare for a rug this age.
direction: Telling the story of Cairo Garden.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: The medallion is a garden seen from above: a pool in the centre, flowers around it. Close knotting for a Cairo piece.
direction: Explaining the craft of Cairo Garden.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Cotton foundation, so it lies flat and keeps its shape. Fifteen years old and nothing has moved.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Bought in the Old City. The seller said it was made for a house near the Damascus Gate, and prayed on for twenty years.
direction: Telling the story of Jerusalem Stone.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Quiet colours, the colour of the city's stone. It is meant to be calm, not to shout.
direction: Explaining the craft of Jerusalem Stone.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Soft wool, well packed. Prayer rugs are made to be knelt on.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: From the plateau near Konya. The villages there weave through the winter, when the snow shuts the roads.
direction: Telling the story of Anatolian Hearth.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Long, lustrous plateau wool and natural dyes. The angles are sharp because the knots are counted, not drawn.
direction: Explaining the craft of Anatolian Hearth.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Anatolian wool is the toughest there is. Sheep that live through that winter grow wool like wire.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Aleppo merchants lay these in their courtyards in summer. The frame is the wall, the bands are the paths.
direction: Telling the story of Aleppo Courtyard.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Balanced, every band answered by another. The Aleppo dealers like a rug you can read.
direction: Explaining the craft of Aleppo Courtyard.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Made for a courtyard, so it takes sun and stone floors.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: From the Hamidiyya in Damascus. The dealer swore the blue came from the last indigo dyer in the city.
direction: Telling the story of Damascus Blue.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Fine wool on cotton, closer knotting than a village rug. Look at the edges of the lozenges: crisp.
direction: Explaining the craft of Damascus Blue.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Fine but not fragile. A dining room, a study, a quiet salon.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: A hundred years old at least, from the Konya weavers. The dervishes there say a good prayer rug keeps the prayers in.
direction: Telling the story of Konya Prayer Rug.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Old natural dyes that have softened with time, and fine wool. You cannot fake that colour; it takes a century.
direction: Explaining the craft of Konya Prayer Rug.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Old, so gently. Hang it or lay it where nobody walks.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: This came from the Maghreb with a French officer. Nobody in Cairo has another one like it, and collectors know it.
direction: Telling the story of Moroccan Ember.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Thick tribal wool and motifs I have never seen on an Egyptian loom. Different hands, different ideas.
direction: Explaining the craft of Moroccan Ember.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Deep pile, made for cold mountain nights. It is warm to stand on.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: This lay in a pasha's salon in Garden City. His heirs divided the house and sold the carpets before the ink was dry.
direction: Telling the story of Golden Palm.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Fine wool with a gold-yellow that only comes from weld and patience. Salon quality.
direction: Explaining the craft of Golden Palm.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: A salon rug: made for receptions and slippers, not boots.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: The Armenian dealers call these eagle rugs. They came out of the Caucasus before the war, and no more are coming.
direction: Telling the story of Caucasus Eagle.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: The birds are pure geometry. Caucasian weavers never copied nature; they counted it.
direction: Explaining the craft of Caucasus Eagle.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Tough mountain wool, but it is old. Treat it with respect.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Persian, around the turn of the century. An Armenian dealer carried it to Cairo and would not sell it for ten years. His widow sold it to Rashid, with his papers.
direction: Telling the story of Sapphire Night.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Fine wool on cotton and very close knotting. The borders are woven without a single mistake.
direction: Explaining the craft of Sapphire Night.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: This came through Damascus from a Persian court workshop. One family kept it for four generations. There are papers, and a seal.
direction: Telling the story of Damascus Rose.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Very fine wool with silk highlights that catch the light. Tilt it, see how it changes.
direction: Explaining the craft of Damascus Rose.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: A carpet for a palace, not a passage. Nobody should walk on it in shoes.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: This left an Istanbul palace household when the Sultanate ended. The steward kept a list of every carpet, and this one is on it.
direction: Telling the story of Istanbul Tulip.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Tulips and carnations, the Ottoman court flowers, with silk highlights. Look at the border: it never loses count.
direction: Explaining the craft of Istanbul Tulip.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Two centuries of care kept it like this. It deserves the same.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: The Persian merchants of Baghdad say it was woven for a prince and carried down the Tigris by night, so nobody would see it leave.
direction: Telling the story of Baghdad Night.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: Very fine wool on a fine foundation, close enough that the drawing looks painted. This is the best weaving I have ever held.
direction: Explaining the craft of Baghdad Night.

speaker: seller
voice_brief: The merchant. Egyptian man, early 40s, deep warm baritone, charming and unhurried, light Cairene accent in English. Smiles through his lines.
text: It belongs in a palace or a museum. A king should decide where it lies.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Good morning. I have been told this corner keeps better rugs than it looks.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Good day. I will not take much of your time, if you will not waste mine.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You are still here. Good. I was afraid the landlord would have taken the corner back.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I came back, you see. That is either a compliment or a warning.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Good morning. Do not look so surprised. I told you I would return if the first one behaved.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I am furnishing a receiving room. I want something beautiful, but not something that announces its price before its taste.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: It is a receiving room with tall windows and dark wood. Everything in it is quiet. The rug must agree with that.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I like things that have come from somewhere. A rug should have a past, and it should be true.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I like a rug that makes a guest ask about it. Not one that answers the question before it is asked.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You ask what I will spend before you know what I want? That is how a hotel buys rugs.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: For the right piece I would go to perhaps ten pounds. For the wrong one, nothing at all.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: My husband signs the cheques. I choose what is on the floor. We are both content with that arrangement.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: It is hot, yes. It was hot yesterday also. Shall we talk about rugs?

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Your cat seems to own the stall. I suspect she chooses the stock.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Thank you. Mint, not too sweet. You remembered, or you guessed well.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You are showing me rugs before you know what I need. Is that how you sell in Giza?

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Now that is interesting. Let me see it properly.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Yes. This one has manners.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: It is a good rug. I am not yet sure it is my rug.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Hmm. Show me the corner.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: No. I can see why someone would want it. It is not me.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is a rug for a hotel lobby.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: The blue is deep without being dark. That would sit well with the wood.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: So much red. It would be the loudest thing in the room.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Pale grounds are elegant, but they are a great deal of work.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Straw colours. Cheerful. Perhaps a little plain for a receiving room.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: The colours argue with each other a little.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: It needs a wash. You are selling me the dust as well?

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: The pile is low along one side. It has had a long life already.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: There is damage in the corner. I can see it from here.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: A caravan sign. A place to rest. That is exactly what a receiving room is for.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is a story I could tell at dinner without sounding like I am boasting.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: A pleasant story. Every rug in this lane has one.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Hmm. I was hoping for something truer.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Yes, I can see the knots. You know your trade.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I am sure the knots are very fine. I will not be counting them.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You sound like a dealer's catalogue.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Yes. Against dark wood and tall windows, I can see it.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You listened. That is rarer than silk in this market.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I am not sure it would be quiet enough.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You are describing a different room from mine.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Good. I do not want to buy another in five years.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: It will last, yes. So would a stone floor. That is not why one buys a rug.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You have told me that already.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Yes, yes. You said so.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: A pasha's house. Well. That would amuse my mother-in-law.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: A pasha's house? A moment ago you had no papers at all. Which is it?

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: You have just told me two different histories. I will believe neither.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Done. Quickly, before you change your mind.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is fair. More than fair.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is reasonable. I accept.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Very well. We have an agreement.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is a Garden City price, and I am standing in Giza.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: No. That is too much for what it is.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Now you are testing me. I did not come here to be tested.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I think the sun has reached your head.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I will give you

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Holding firm is not the same as being right.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Then we are both standing still.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Delivered to the house and the fringe washed? That makes a difference.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I have another appointment at noon.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Let us come to it, please.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Send it to the house on Sharia Qasr el-Nil by the afternoon. You have done well.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Good. It will be the first thing in that room I have not had to argue with.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I bought it. I am not certain why.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: No. Thank you for your time, but no.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I think I will look elsewhere today.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: Your cat is sitting on the one I wanted to see. She has taste.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: My sister is furnishing her study and asked me who sold me that rug. She wants something quieter still. Keep an eye out for her.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is exactly what she needs. She will be delighted. So will I, for being right.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: I have told two friends about your corner. Behave yourself.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: That is not a Giza rug. Where did you find it?

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: My cousin knows the old families. He says no pasha ever owned that rug. I would have liked the truth better.

speaker: samira
voice_brief: Samira. Egyptian woman, early 30s, refined upper-class Cairo accent, calm and precise, dry wit, never raises her voice.
text: The rug you sold me worked beautifully in the receiving room. My sister is now looking for something quieter.

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

speaker: hassan

text: Hurry, hurry, the coffee will boil over.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Come tonight, the first coffee is free. And tell nobody what I paid.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Good. Now it is a real coffee house.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Well, I bought it. The men will tell me if it was a mistake.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Not today, my friend. Come for coffee instead.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: I will think. Thinking is free.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: The cat likes it! A cat knows a good rug. I will take her word.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: The doorway needs a runner. Tough, warm. Find me one and I pay a bonus, and the coffee is free for a month.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: There it is. Now even my doorway is respectable. Here is your bonus.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: I sent the tailor from next door. He talks too much, be patient.

speaker: hassan

text: That is not a coffee-house rug. That is a museum.

speaker: hassan

voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: The last rug? The customers pray on it now.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Now you speak like a friend.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Your cat is fatter than my cat. You feed her too well.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Silk? In my coffee house? The backgammon players would eat it alive.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Ha! An honest man. Show me something tough.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Strong, you say. Stronger than a Saidi with a nargileh? I doubt it.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Pale as milk. By Thursday it will be the colour of my coffee.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: At least you say it. What else have you got?

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: You can wash it? Who washes, me?

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: It is already dirty. You want me to pay for somebody else's coffee?

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Good, then we talk about the price.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Under the dirt it is good, you say. Everyone says that.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Tell me honestly. Why should a coffee-house man pay for this and not for a mat from the Wednesday market?

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Now that is a good answer. I like a man who does not pretend.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Ten years? My last rug lasted three. We will see.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Forty men a night on my floor, and every one of them spills something. I need a rug that forgives, like a good wife.
direction: A floor rug for the coffee house

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Good morning. I am told you are the honest one in this lane. We shall see.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Hello. Please don't start with "for you, special price". Everyone does.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Good morning again. I wrote to my sister about your last rug. She was quite envious.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I'm back, as you see. I seem to have caught the carpet fever.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: A small bedroom in a house in Surrey, eventually. For now, a very large house in Zamalek.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: The schoolroom has a marble floor and three children who treat it as a racecourse.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I want something with a real history. Not "a pasha's palace". A real one.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Something I can describe in a letter without sounding like an advertisement.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Goodness, you are direct. Let us see what you have first.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I had thought about five pounds. For something truly special, the Pasha's budget runs to fourteen.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I decide. There is nobody else. That is rather the point of being a governess.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: The heat is quite unreasonable, isn't it? The children think it is hilarious that I melt.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I have been reading about the Mamluks. Terribly violent people, but such beautiful carpets.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Tea! How very civilised. Thank you, I would love some.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh. You haven't asked me anything yet. How do you know what I want?

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh, that is lovely. May I touch it?

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Now that is exactly the sort of thing I meant.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: It is very nice. I'm not sure it is me.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Hm. Tell me about it.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh dear, no. That is rather loud for a governess.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I don't think my sister would forgive me.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Such a lovely blue. Like the sky over the Nile in the evening.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Very red. Rather Victorian.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Pale and light. That would look well in a small room.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Like sand. Very Egyptian.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Lots going on. The children would enjoy it, I suppose.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: It does need a wash, doesn't it?

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: It has been loved, that one.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh, there's a tear. What a shame.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh, how wonderful. Tell me more, I want to get it right in my letter.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: That is a much better story than the guidebook.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: That is a nice story. Is it true?

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I had no idea the knots were counted. How patient they must be.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I'm afraid knots are a little beyond me.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I can see it by the window in the schoolroom. Yes.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: That would fit in a trunk and still be the best thing in the house.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I'm not sure it would suit.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Anything that survives these three children will survive anything.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I'm less worried about it lasting than about liking it.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Yes, you did say.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I remember, thank you.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: A pasha's palace! My sister will be beside herself.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: A pasha? Oh dear. You had just said you had no papers. Please don't.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh, that's very fair. Yes, please.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Done. How exciting.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: That seems fair. Very well.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: All right. Yes. I shall have it.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh, that's rather more than I hoped.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I'm afraid that is beyond a governess.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe

voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I'm sorry, I'm rather short of time.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Thank you. I shall write to my sister tonight.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Wonderful. I feel I have finally bought something real.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Well, I have bought it. I hope I shan't regret it.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Thank you, but not today.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh, the cat! Isn't she magnificent? She can stay.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: My sister writes that she wants one too, small, with a true story. I don't suppose you could find one?

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour

speaker: whitcombe

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: That is very kind of you.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: May I? Oh, she purrs like a motorcar.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Forgive me, but this looks rather like the carpets in my aunt's house in Guildford.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Thank you for not pretending. I did wonder.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Hand-knotted, you say? The back looks very even.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh dear. It could do with a good wash, couldn't it?

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Well, that is honest. Perhaps with a little off the price.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: A wash will bring it up? I shall have to trust you.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: And where exactly does it come from? I do like to know what I'm writing home about.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I appreciate a man who admits what he doesn't know. It is rarer than you would think here.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Hm. That sounds a little like a guidebook.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I must be sensible. A governess is not a duchess, whatever the children think.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Thank you. That is refreshingly straightforward.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: It will last a lifetime? Well. I suppose that is a sort of economy.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I sail for England in the summer, for good this time, I think. I want one real Egyptian thing to put by my bed. Small enough for a trunk.

speaker: whitcombe

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Good day. Rashid tells me your father knew rugs. Let us see if you do.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Good morning. I have a quarter of an hour between patients.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Good day again. The last rug has calmed three hundred patients. I counted.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I am back. That is a compliment; I do not go back to many shops.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: My consulting room on Emad el-Din. Frightened people, a desk, a window onto a noisy street.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: A room where people tell me their troubles. It must be calm.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Fine work. Honest provenance. And if possible, something from Anatolia or the Caucasus.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I grew up near looms. I like to see a weaver's hand in a rug.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: You ask the price before the patient's symptoms? That is bad medicine.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: For the right rug, ten or twelve pounds. For the one I dream of, eighteen, and not a piastre more.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I decide. My wife has better taste, but she trusts me with rugs, if not with hats.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Cairo is kind to us. Kinder than some places. I do not forget that.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I read that the League of Nations is talking about us again. Talking is what they do best.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Thank you. My mother made tea like this in Aintab.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: You show me a rug before you know what I need. A diagnosis before the examination.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Ah. May I turn it over? Yes. Yes, this is good.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: That is fine work. Look at the edges.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: It is a rug. It is not a remarkable rug.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Tell me why I should look at it twice.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: No. That would frighten my patients.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Please. Show me something with care in it.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Blue. The colour of calm. Good.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Madder red. Like home.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Pale. Beautiful, but the street will ruin it.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Too cheerful for a consulting room.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Many colours. My patients are anxious enough.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: It needs cleaning. I will not bring dirt into a doctor's room.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Worn. Honest wear, at least.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: There is damage. I see damage all day.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: That is a story I can believe. Go on.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: My mother used to tell stories like that about rugs.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: A nice story. Does the rug agree with it?

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Yes, the knot count is high. You know what you are talking about.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Natural dyes. You can see the abrash. Good.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I know how rugs are made. Tell me about this one.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I can see it in front of my desk. The patients would look at it and breathe.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Not for a consulting room.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: It will last. Good. I intend to practise for another twenty years.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Durability is the least of my worries.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: You said that already.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I heard you the first time.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: A pasha's palace? Well. It is possible.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: A pasha's palace? You said a moment ago you had no papers. Please. I have heard enough lies in my life.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: That is fair. More than fair. Thank you.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Done. You are an honest man, or a foolish one.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary

speaker: benakis

text: Back again! My guests still talk about the last one.

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

text: The salon. It has to say: this man is very successful. Subtly. Or not subtly.

speaker: benakis

text: Something rare. Something my rivals at the Cotton Exchange do not have.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: I want people to ask "where did you get that?" and I want to smile and not tell them.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Money? Plenty. But I do not like to waste it. Show me first.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My wife decides the curtains. I decide the carpets. We have an arrangement.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Cotton is up four points this week. I am in a very good mood.

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

text: It is fine. I do not buy fine.

speaker: benakis

speaker: benakis

text: Please. I came on the first-class train.

speaker: benakis

text: Ivory. My wife would love it. The dogs would ruin it.

voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Gold! Yes. Gold is always right.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: It is dirty. Do you know who I am?

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: A story! My guests will love it. Tell me everything.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Wonderful. I will tell this story at dinner and make it better.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Stories are nice. Rarity is better.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Very fine. I can see the work. Expensive work.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Knots. Yes. Very clever.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: In the salon, under the chandelier. Salvago will die.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Yes, I see it. It would make the whole room.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Not quite the villa, my friend.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: It lasts forever? Good, then I only buy it once. Though I like buying.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My friend, I do not buy rugs to last. I buy rugs to impress.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Yes, yes, you told me. I listen, I promise.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: I heard. Go on.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: A pasha's palace! Of course. I knew it the moment I saw it.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: A pasha? You just told me you have no papers. Do not play Greek with a Greek.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Done! Wrap it before I come to my senses.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Done, done. You should charge more, you know.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis

voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Well. I bought it. I will say it came from Istanbul.

text: Not today, my friend. Not today.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: I will look at the Khan. Adio.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: A cat on the carpet. Get it off, please, I am allergic to cats and to poverty.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My rival Salvago has a salon carpet the whole of Alexandria talks about. Find me something better. Exceptional, ornate. I will pay a very good bonus.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Yes! Salvago is finished. Here, take this, and do not tell anyone how much.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: I told the Salvagos about you. Be expensive with them.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Now this. Where did this come from?

speaker: benakis

text: My guests still ask about the last one. I tell them I found it in Persia.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: You see? We are friends now.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Keep that animal away from my suit, please.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My friend, my servants walk on rugs like this.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Ha! Honest. I like you. Show me the good things.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Well made, yes, yes. Still a servant's rug.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: You show me a dirty rug? Me?

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: At least you do not pretend. Clean it and show me again.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Underneath, perfect, you say. I will believe it when I see it.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Salvago has a better one than this. Much better. I have seen it.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: You say this is finer? Then Salvago will choke on his cigar.

speaker: benakis

speaker: salem
text: Peace be upon you. They told me at the camel market there is a rug man here who does not shout.

speaker: salem
text: Peace upon you. I have sold my camels. Now I have money and no patience for liars.

speaker: salem
text: Peace upon you again. Your last rug crossed the Canal with me and did not complain once.

speaker: salem
text: I came back. In Sinai we say a well you trust is worth the long walk.

speaker: salem
text: My tent near Nuweiba. Goat hair, a fire, and whoever God sends to sit by it.

speaker: salem
text: The guest side of the tent. Where the coffee is poured and the men talk until the stars go.

speaker: salem
text: Something that lasts. Wool, strong, not too proud of itself.

speaker: salem

speaker: salem
text: You ask a man his purse before you ask his name? Slowly, my son.

speaker: salem
text: For a good rug, ten pounds. For one that outlives me, fifteen, and no more.

speaker: salem
text: I decide. My wife will tell me afterwards if I decided well. She usually says no.

speaker: salem
text: The Frontier Administration wants a paper for every camel. Soon they will want a paper for every flea.

speaker: salem
text: They closed the Parliament in March, I hear. In the desert we never opened one, and we still argue.

speaker: salem
text: A Cairo man asked me how many camels I own. I asked him how many rooms his house has. We were both rude.

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem
text: Now this has a face. Let me put my hand on it.

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem
text: This is for a pasha with slippers. I have none.

speaker: salem

speaker: salem
text: Red. Red is honest. It hides the dust and keeps the eye warm.

speaker: salem
text: White. You have never seen a goat, I think.

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem
text: Tell it slowly. A story told fast is a lie in a hurry.

speaker: salem
text: Good. I will tell that one by the fire.

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

speaker: salem

text: My guest tent wants a true caravan rug. Hard-wearing, a rug that has travelled or can. Find me one and I pay you over the price.

speaker: salem
text: That is it. A rug for guests and for the road. Here, take this, with my thanks.

speaker: salem
text: I told a man from the Frontier Administration about you. He is an Englishman who thinks he knows camels. Be patient.

speaker: salem
text: Now you speak like a host.

speaker: salem
text: A good animal. In the desert she would eat better, and work harder.

speaker: salem
text: This is a rug for a man who never sits on the ground. I sit on the ground.

speaker: salem
text: Good. You know it. Now show me what a Bedouin can use.

speaker: salem
text: Strong, you say. I have heard silk called many things. Never strong.

speaker: salem
text: Pale. The desert will make it brown in one night, and the goats in one hour.

speaker: salem
text: At least you do not tell me it stays white.

speaker: salem
text: You wash it? In the desert we save water for the camels.

speaker: salem
text: Very busy, this one. A guest should look at my face, not at the floor.

speaker: salem
text: Ha. You agree too quickly. But you agree honestly.

speaker: salem
text: Fine work, yes. Fine work is for people with roofs.

speaker: salem
text: The camel trader at Imbaba cheated me yesterday with a smile. Why should your price be different?

speaker: salem
text: Because you did not smile. Good. We can talk.

speaker: salem
text: It will last my lifetime and my son's? Then perhaps it is cheap. Perhaps.

speaker: salem
text: I go back across the Canal next week. I want a rug that rolls onto a camel, keeps the cold off at night, and does not complain.

speaker: levy
text: Bonjour. Sabah el-kheir. I have four stalls to see before lunch. Yours is the first.

speaker: levy
text: Good morning. I am Rachel Lévy, from Alexandria. I buy, I do not browse.

speaker: levy
text: Bonjour again. Your last rug sold in nine days. That is why I am here.

speaker: levy
text: Back, as you see. My manager asked for more of the same.

speaker: levy
text: A carpet department on Rue Chérif Pacha. Forty rugs on the floor, twenty in the basement, and one window.

speaker: levy
text: Clients who come in for curtains and leave with a carpet. If I have chosen well.

speaker: levy
text: Rugs I can sell twice. Once to the client, and once again when her sister sees it.

speaker: levy
text: Handsome, well made, and a pattern the weavers can make again next year.

speaker: levy
text: Good, a man who asks. Seven pounds for stock, up to twenty-five for the window. Now show me.

speaker: levy
text: Between seven and twenty-five pounds, depending. I told you already. I like that you asked.

speaker: levy
text: I decide. My manager signs. It is the same thing, but he likes to hold the pen.

speaker: levy
text: Cotton is falling again. When cotton falls, Alexandria buys smaller rugs.

speaker: levy
text: Everyone in Alexandria wants the Paris look since the Exposition. Straight lines, pale colours. It will pass.

speaker: levy
text: Half my clients want a Tutankhamun rug. I tell them the pharaoh sat on reeds.

speaker: levy

speaker: levy

speaker: levy

speaker: levy

speaker: levy

speaker: levy

speaker: levy

speaker: antonios
text: Peace to you, my son. I have come a long way on the tram, so be patient with an old man.

speaker: antonios
text: Good morning. A parishioner at Giza is sick, and I thought, while I am here, I will look at carpets.

speaker: antonios
text: Peace to you again. The last rug is behaving itself. Better than some of my altar boys.

speaker: antonios
text: I am back. Do not look so pleased, it is the committee who sent me.

speaker: antonios
text: Our church stands inside the old Roman walls, by the gate of the Babylon fortress. Low, dark, very old. The Holy Family rested near there, we believe.

speaker: antonios
text: The steps to the sanctuary. Every soul in the parish walks up them, and some of them are very heavy souls.

speaker: antonios
text: Something quiet. Something that has worked for its living. I do not trust a rug that shouts.

speaker: antonios
text: Wool, a dark ground, and an honest account of where it has been. That is all I ask.

speaker: antonios
text: Money, already? Let us first see if God has put the right rug in your shop.

speaker: antonios
text: For the steps, perhaps ten pounds. For the bishop's room, the widow left up to twenty. Not a coin more, and I will know.

speaker: antonios
text: I choose. The committee complains. Then after a year they say it was their idea. That is how committees work.

speaker: antonios
text: They say they found gold in the King's tomb at Luxor. We have had old things in Old Cairo for centuries, and nobody sends a newspaper.

speaker: antonios
text: The Parliament met one day and was sent home the same evening. I have given longer sermons than that.

speaker: antonios
text: Tea, thank you. With a little sugar. At my age the doctor says no sugar, so a little.

speaker: antonios
text: Already a rug? You have not asked me where it will lie. Is it for a church or a coffee house?

speaker: antonios
text: Ah. Yes. That is a rug that knows how to be quiet.

speaker: antonios
text: Let me sit a moment and look at it. Yes. This has a good soul.

speaker: antonios
text: It is a decent rug. I am not yet sure it is a church rug.

speaker: antonios
text: Hmm. Turn it over for me, please. My knees are not what they were.

speaker: antonios
text: Oh, my son. The bishop would think I had joined the theatre.

speaker: antonios
text: No, no. That belongs in a dancing hall, God forgive me for knowing what one looks like.

speaker: antonios
text: Blue. The colour of the Virgin's robe in our icons. Good.

speaker: antonios
text: Deep red, like the old vestments. That is a church colour.

speaker: antonios
text: White. Beautiful, and in one week the whole parish will have written on it with their shoes.

speaker: antonios
text: Sandy gold. Warm, but a little worldly for the sanctuary.

speaker: antonios
text: Many colours, quietly together. Like a good congregation, when it behaves.

speaker: antonios
text: It needs washing. So do we all, before Easter.

speaker: antonios
text: It is worn. So am I. We may still be useful.

speaker: antonios
text: There is damage. A church floor would finish it.

speaker: antonios
text: That is a good story, and I think a true one. Tell it again slowly.

speaker: antonios
text: Ah. I may put that in a sermon, if you do not mind.

speaker: antonios
text: A pleasant story. But the floor does not listen to stories.

speaker: antonios
text: Patient hands made this. Patience is a virtue, and this rug has a great deal of it.

speaker: antonios
text: I am a priest, my son, not a weaver. Tell me if it will last.

speaker: antonios
text: I can see it before the sanctuary screen, under the old lamps. Yes. The icons would approve.

speaker: antonios
text: I do not think it suits a church. Perhaps a bank.

speaker: antonios
text: Strong. Good. Then I will not have to come back here before I die.

speaker: antonios
text: That is what I wanted to hear. Our floors are stone, and our people are many.

speaker: antonios
text: Strong, yes. But a church needs more than strength.

speaker: antonios
text: You said so, my son. I am old, but not yet deaf.

speaker: antonios
text: Yes, I heard. Once is enough, as with confession.

speaker: antonios
text: A patriarch's palace! Well, well. God moves in mysterious ways, and so do carpets.

speaker: antonios
text: A patriarch's palace? You told me a moment ago you did not know where it came from. My son, lying to a priest is two sins at once.

speaker: antonios
text: That is generous. God will remember it, even if the committee does not.

speaker: antonios
text: Done, and may your house be blessed.

speaker: antonios
text: That is fair. The widow would agree. Done.

speaker: antonios
text: Very well. Fair to you, fair to the church. Done.

speaker: antonios
text: That is a price for a cathedral in Paris, not a little church in Old Cairo.

speaker: antonios
text: Too much, my son. The widow was generous, not foolish.

speaker: antonios
text: My son, I have heard many confessions. Few were as shameless as that price.

speaker: antonios
text: God forgive you. I will try, but it will take some time.

speaker: antonios

speaker: antonios
text: God bless you, my son. Come to the liturgy one Sunday and see it lying there.

speaker: antonios
text: Good. Now the church floor has a new servant. Thank you.

speaker: antonios
text: Well. It is bought. I will pray that I was right.

speaker: antonios
text: Not today, my son. Peace be with you.

speaker: antonios
text: I will pray on it. Prayer is slower than bargaining, but it is cheaper.

speaker: antonios
text: Ah, the cat approves! We have three at the church. They keep the mice from the old books, and they sleep on the warm rugs.

speaker: antonios
text: The nave has an old runner down the middle, older than me. When you find something quiet, dark and strong, a real rug, not a mat, bring it to me. The committee will add something for your trouble.

speaker: antonios
text: That is exactly right. It does its work and says nothing. Here, the committee's thanks, and mine.

speaker: antonios
text: I told a family from our parish about you. They are poor but honest. Be kind to them.

speaker: antonios
text: That is too fine for a church floor. That is for a museum, or for heaven.

speaker: antonios
text: A deacon of ours knew that rug you called a patriarch's. There was no patriarch. I have confessed my part in it. Have you?

speaker: antonios
text: The last rug? The old women say the church looks younger. I say nothing, in case it goes to its head.

speaker: antonios
text: That is kind. Kindness is never wasted, my son.

speaker: antonios
text: A fine cat. She has the look of a church cat, very pleased with herself.

speaker: antonios
text: It is very beautiful, my son. Too beautiful. The people would look at the floor and not at the altar.

speaker: antonios
text: You understand. A church is not a pasha's salon. Show me something quieter.

speaker: antonios
text: Yes, yes, it is well made. So is a gold watch. I still do not wear one to the liturgy.

speaker: antonios
text: It has been badly treated, this one. I would have to answer to the committee for every mark.

speaker: antonios
text: Thank you for not hiding it. The committee will like a lower price even more than a clean rug.

speaker: antonios
text: It will wash clean? Well, so do sinners, with patience. Perhaps.

speaker: antonios
text: And where did it come from? A rug for a church should not have a past it is ashamed of.

speaker: antonios
text: You do not know. Good. An honest not knowing is better than a clever story.

speaker: antonios
text: That sounds like something a man says because it is useful to say.

speaker: antonios
text: This is not my money, you understand. It is the widow's mite. I must be able to look her grave in the face.

speaker: antonios
text: Thank you for speaking plainly. We will find a price that does not trouble anyone's sleep.

speaker: antonios
text: Twenty years of feet, you say. Then it costs the church less each year. I can tell the committee that.

speaker: antonios
text: The steps before the sanctuary are worn into dips by eight hundred years of feet. The old runner has finally gone to God. I need a new one, long, dark and strong.
direction: A runner for the sanctuary steps

speaker: antonios

direction: A rug for the bishop's reception room

speaker: wasif
text: Good morning. I pass your stall every Friday on the way to my villa. Today I decided to stop and cross-examine you.

speaker: wasif
text: Good day. I am told you do not lie. I am a lawyer, so I shall test that.

speaker: wasif
text: Good morning again. The last carpet has survived three dinners and one Minister. Well done.

speaker: wasif
text: I am back. Consider it a second hearing.

speaker: wasif
text: My study on the Qasr el-Nil. Books on every wall, a window onto the street, and clients who talk too much.

speaker: wasif
text: A room where men come to tell me the truth, eventually. The carpet should help them.

speaker: wasif
text: Old work. Fine work. And papers I could read to a judge without blushing.

speaker: wasif
text: I collect carpets the way I collect evidence. The good ones speak for themselves, and the documents confirm it.

speaker: wasif
text: The fee before the facts? You would make a poor lawyer and a rich dealer.

speaker: wasif
text: For the study, twenty-five pounds, perhaps forty. For a true collector's piece with papers, I would go to eighty. Not further.

speaker: wasif
text: I decide. My wife advises. In my house, as in court, the advice is usually right.

speaker: wasif
text: Parliament met in March and was dissolved the same day. A record. I believe even the English were embarrassed.

speaker: wasif
text: Mr Carter has quarrelled with the Antiquities Service over the tomb. He needed a better lawyer. I was available.

speaker: wasif
text: Tea. Thank you. My clerk makes it too weak. This is proper.

speaker: wasif
text: You present exhibits before you know the charge. Ask me what I want first.

speaker: wasif
text: Now that is a serious carpet. Let me see the back.

speaker: wasif
text: Yes. That has the look of something that has been properly owned.

speaker: wasif
text: It is competent. I do not collect competence.

speaker: wasif
text: Make your case for it. Briefly.

speaker: wasif
text: No. My clerk has a better one in his flat in Shubra.

speaker: wasif
text: I think you have mistaken me for a tourist from Shepheard's.

speaker: wasif
text: A good indigo. Deep, serious. It would suit a room full of law books.

speaker: wasif
text: Madder red, well aged. The colour of the wax seal on a good deed.

speaker: wasif
text: Ivory. Elegant, and hopeless in a room where men smoke.

speaker: wasif
text: Gold. A little eager to please.

speaker: wasif
text: A crowded palette. Like a courtroom on a Monday.

speaker: wasif
text: It is dirty. The court will note it in mitigation of price.

speaker: wasif
text: Worn. Age I accept. Neglect I charge for.

speaker: wasif
text: Damaged. That is not character, that is evidence of mistreatment.

speaker: wasif
text: That is a good account, and it hangs together. Go on.

speaker: wasif
text: Names, places, dates. At last, a story with witnesses.

speaker: wasif
text: A charming tale. I have heard better from clients who were later convicted.

speaker: wasif
text: Yes. The knotting is close and the drawing never slips. That is the carpet testifying for itself.

speaker: wasif
text: Natural dyes, and the colour has softened evenly. Good. Hard to fake.

speaker: wasif
text: I can count knots as well as you. Tell me something I cannot see.

speaker: wasif
text: In front of the bookcases, under the lamp. A client would sit there and tell me everything.

speaker: wasif
text: It would not suit the study. Or me.

speaker: wasif
text: It will outlast me. Good; my son will inherit something besides my debts.

speaker: wasif
text: I do not buy carpets to walk on. I buy them to look at.

speaker: wasif
text: You made that argument already. Repetition is not evidence.

speaker: wasif
text: Noted, the first time.

speaker: wasif
text: The Khedive's own palace? That would be remarkable. I shall make enquiries.

speaker: wasif
text: The Khedive's palace? A moment ago you admitted you had no papers. You have just impeached your own witness.

speaker: wasif
text: That is a fair price. Suspiciously fair. Done, before you appeal.

speaker: wasif
text: Agreed. You have undervalued it, and I shall not tell you by how much.

speaker: wasif
text: A reasonable figure. Agreed.

speaker: wasif
text: Fair. Let us not waste the court's time. Done.

speaker: wasif
text: That is not a price, that is an opening statement.

speaker: wasif
text: Too high. Even a Mixed Court judgment is cheaper.

speaker: wasif
text: I have seen more modest claims from the British Treasury.

speaker: wasif
text: Case dismissed. Good day.
