speaker: martel
text: That is gracious of you.

speaker: martel
text: A handsome cat. She has the air of an ambassador.

speaker: martel
text: It is a little loud, I think. One does not shout in a reception room.

speaker: martel
text: You agree. Good. Then let us look at something quieter.

speaker: martel
text: Vigorous, yes. Vigour is not what I need.

speaker: martel
text: And its history? A gift with a doubtful past can become a small scandal.

speaker: martel
text: Thank you for your frankness. It is worth more to me than a fine story.

speaker: martel
text: You tell it well. I am not sure a Damascene family would hear it the same way.

speaker: martel
text: There is some damage here. One cannot give a damaged gift.

speaker: martel
text: You do not hide it. That is correct of you.

speaker: martel
text: It can be restored, you say. Then show it to me restored.

speaker: martel
text: I will be frank. The Republic is not generous with its diplomats. Is this price serious?

speaker: martel
text: Good. We understand each other.

speaker: martel
text: A fair argument. I will put it in my report.

speaker: martel
text: I must make a gift to a gentleman in Damascus. An old family. The gift must honour him, and it must say nothing too loudly.
direction: A gift for a Syrian notable

speaker: martel
text: The reception room of our residence in Beirut. Ministers, consuls, a great many opinions. The carpet should have none.

speaker: rustam
text: Peace be upon you. I am Rustam, from Baghdad, and from Isfahan before that. We are in the same trade, you and I.

speaker: rustam
text: Good morning, colleague. I came by the Nairn cars to Damascus, then the train. I hope your rugs are worth the dust.

speaker: rustam
text: Good morning again. The last rug sold well in Paris. I will not tell you how well.

speaker: rustam
text: I am back. That is the best praise one merchant can give another.

speaker: rustam
text: A warehouse on the Tigris, full of bales. And a small room above it where I drink tea with men who buy.

speaker: rustam
text: My rugs do not stay in any room. They go to Paris, to London, to men who pay in pounds.

speaker: rustam
text: Close knotting, true colours, honest papers. And Persian, if God is kind.

speaker: rustam
text: I buy what I can sell again. A rug with a true history sells itself.

speaker: rustam
text: You ask a merchant his purse? I will ask you your cost. Then we are even.

speaker: rustam
text: For a good piece, twenty-five or thirty pounds. For a rare one with papers, a hundred, perhaps more.

speaker: rustam
text: I decide. My brother keeps the books in Baghdad, and he complains, but I decide.

speaker: rustam
text: The League's commission has been in Mosul all year, asking the villages who they want to belong to. The Turks want it, the English want the oil.

speaker: rustam
text: Baghdad to Damascus now takes one day by motor car, across the open desert. The camel men are not pleased.

speaker: rustam
text: Saadi says the sons of Adam are limbs of one body. The customs men at the frontier have not read him.

speaker: rustam
text: Thank you. Tea is the start of every honest bargain. And most of the dishonest ones.

speaker: rustam
text: A rug already? You have not asked what I buy. Never mind. Show me.

speaker: rustam
text: Ah. Let me look at the back. Yes. Yes, this is a real carpet.

speaker: rustam
text: Now we are talking as merchants. That is good work.

speaker: rustam
text: It is a rug. I have a warehouse of rugs.

speaker: rustam
text: Hm. Tell me why a Parisian would want it.

speaker: rustam
text: No. I could buy that in the Baghdad souq for the price of lunch.

speaker: rustam
text: Please. I did not cross the desert for this.

speaker: rustam
text: Good indigo. Deep, even. That is money in Paris.

speaker: rustam
text: Madder red. The colour the French always ask for.

speaker: rustam
text: A pale ground. Beautiful, and one muddy boot will ruin my profit.

speaker: rustam
text: Yellow from weld. Pretty. It fades, you know.

speaker: rustam
text: Many colours. If they are natural, good. Let me see in the sun.

speaker: rustam
text: Dirty. The washer costs money.

speaker: rustam
text: Worn low. Honest, but it lowers the price.

speaker: rustam
text: Damaged. A repair in Paris costs more than the rug.

speaker: rustam
text: That story I believe. The rug agrees with it.

speaker: rustam
text: Good. A true story is worth a pound or two in Paris.

speaker: rustam
text: A pleasant story. Does anybody have it in writing?

speaker: rustam
text: Yes, the knot count is high and the rows are straight. You know what you have.

speaker: rustam
text: You are right about the dyes. Look at the abrash. No chemist made that.

speaker: rustam
text: I know how carpets are woven. My grandfather wove them. Tell me about this one.

speaker: rustam
text: Yes, I know a buyer for this. A villa on the Riviera.

speaker: rustam
text: My rugs have no room. They have a buyer.

speaker: rustam
text: It will survive the voyage and the Paris damp. Good.

speaker: rustam
text: My buyers do not walk on rugs. They hang them.

speaker: rustam
text: You said so already.

speaker: rustam
text: Yes. I heard. I remember everything that concerns money.

speaker: rustam
text: A pasha's house. Well. It is possible.

speaker: rustam
text: A pasha? Saadi said it: musk proves itself by its scent, not by what the perfumer says. You had no papers a moment ago.

speaker: rustam
text: Done. You should not sell to merchants so cheaply, colleague.

speaker: rustam
text: Agreed. And I will not tell anyone what I paid.

speaker: rustam
text: That is a fair price. Agreed.

speaker: rustam
text: Very well. We both make a little. Agreed.

speaker: rustam
text: That is the price I would ask in Paris. I cannot also pay it in Cairo.

speaker: rustam
text: Too much. Where is my profit?

speaker: rustam
text: I am a Persian carpet merchant. I sell that price to tourists myself.

speaker: rustam
text: No. Good day, colleague.

text: Forgive me. A dealer from Smyrna is waiting at the Khan.

speaker: rustam

speaker: rustam
text: Agreed. Send it to Shepheard's, in my name. You will see me again.

speaker: rustam
text: Well. I paid too much. Next time I will be the clever one.

speaker: rustam
text: Not today. But I will come back next winter.

speaker: rustam

speaker: rustam
text: A cat on the carpets. In Isfahan every good dealer has one. She knows the best rug before we do.

speaker: rustam
text: My English client wants one more. Persian, finely woven, with real papers. Find it and I will pay a generous bonus, merchant to merchant.

speaker: rustam
text: Persian, fine and documented. He will be pleased, and so am I. Here is your share.

speaker: rustam
text: I told a Syrian colleague at the Khan about you. He is not honest. Hold your price.

speaker: rustam
text: This one. Where did you find it? Never mind. You will not tell me, and you are right.

speaker: rustam
text: My buyer in Paris asked about that pasha. There was no pasha. I lost face, and a client.

speaker: rustam
text: That is generous, between merchants.

speaker: rustam
text: A fine animal. Persian blood somewhere, I think.

speaker: rustam
text: And the papers? I sell to men who ask. If I cannot answer them, the rug is worth half.

speaker: rustam
text: Good. You do not know, and you say so. I will price it that way.

speaker: rustam
text: A fine story. I tell stories too, in Paris. That is why I do not believe them.

speaker: rustam
text: This is honest bazaar work. In Paris they will call it a floor covering and offer me a franc.

speaker: rustam
text: You know your stock. That is worth more to me than the rug.

speaker: rustam
text: You praise it well. I still cannot sell it in the Rue Drouot.

speaker: rustam
text: It needs washing and a repair. That is my money and my time, not yours.

speaker: rustam
text: Then we take the cost of the washer off the price. Fair.

speaker: rustam
text: Sound under the dirt, you say. Let me turn it over. Hm. Perhaps.

speaker: rustam
text: You understand, I must sell it again. If I pay your price, I have bought a rug and lost a winter.

speaker: rustam
text: You see it as I see it. Good. Merchants can talk.

speaker: rustam
text: The knotting is good, yes. Good knotting is why I came. It is not why I should pay double.

speaker: rustam
text: A dealer in the Rue Drouot writes to me for fine carpets. Since the Exposition, Paris wants the East again. I need one I can sell at a profit, so I cannot pay your full price.
direction: A good piece to resell in Paris

speaker: rustam
text: An English oil man came to my warehouse in Baghdad. Since the concession was signed in March, his company has money. He wants one old carpet with papers. Persian if possible. He pays well, and so will I.
direction: A documented piece for a collector

speaker: shivakiar
text: Bonjour. They tell me the best carpets in Cairo are at Giza, of all places. I came to see if they lie.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Good morning. Do not bow so low, you will hurt your back, and then who will show me the carpets?

speaker: shivakiar
text: I am back, as you see. My guests have not stopped asking where I found the last one.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Bonjour again. You have become a habit, monsieur. A costly one.

speaker: shivakiar
text: My palace on the river. The ballroom is gold and mirrors, and the floor has been waiting for something worthy.

speaker: shivakiar
text: The great salon, where the whole of Cairo comes on my Thursdays. It must be beautiful. Nothing else will do.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Silk, if you have it. Something from a court. Something nobody else in Cairo can buy.

speaker: shivakiar
text: I want my guests to stop talking when they see it. That is very hard, in Cairo.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Money? One does not ask a princess her price, monsieur. One shows her the carpet.

speaker: shivakiar
text: My steward tells me two or three hundred pounds. For the right carpet, I shall not listen to my steward.

speaker: shivakiar
text: I decide. My steward pays, and sighs. It is his only exercise.

speaker: shivakiar
text: They say Parliament is closed and nobody knows when it will open. Luckily, my salon never closes.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Everyone at dinner talks of the tomb at Luxor. I am told the young king had better carpets than any of us.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Paris was full of the Exposition this summer. Everything was Egyptian. We are the fashion, apparently.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Tea. How kind. In a glass? Charmant. I have not drunk tea from a glass since I was a girl.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Already? You do not ask what the carpet is for? In a salon, that would be a faux pas.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Ah. Now that is something. Bring it into the light.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Oh, yes. Ça, c'est magnifique.

speaker: shivakiar
text: It is agreeable. I do not buy agreeable.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Pretty. Is it special, or only pretty?

speaker: shivakiar
text: No, no. Please put it away before my ladies see it.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Monsieur, I did not drive to Giza for that.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Deep blue. Very elegant, by candlelight.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Crimson. Royal. It will look well with the gilt.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Ivory. Pure. My guests would think twice before spilling champagne.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Gold. Of course, gold. Gold is never wrong in a ballroom.

speaker: shivakiar
text: So many colours. Like a garden party. Rather gay.

speaker: shivakiar
text: It needs washing. How disappointing.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Worn. The old families like worn. I prefer perfect.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Damaged? For me? Non.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Oh, lovely. I shall tell it at dinner, and make it better.

speaker: shivakiar
text: That is a story for a ball. Tell me again, slowly.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Charming. Is any of it true?

speaker: shivakiar
text: Yes, I can see the work. It looks painted, not woven.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Knots. How clever of them. Is it beautiful?

speaker: shivakiar
text: In the ballroom, beneath the great chandelier. Yes. I can see the ambassadors staring.

speaker: shivakiar
text: That would make the salon. Tout à fait.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Not for my house, I think.

speaker: shivakiar
text: It will last? Good. My granddaughters may give balls on it.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Monsieur, I do not buy carpets for their endurance. I buy them for their effect.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Yes, you told me. I listen better than people think.

speaker: shivakiar
text: You said so. Go on.

speaker: shivakiar
text: A palace! But of course. One can always tell.

speaker: shivakiar
text: A palace? You just told me you had no papers. Please. I have lived among palaces all my life, and they keep records.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Done. You undervalue yourself, monsieur. I shall not tell you so twice.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Agreed. How very easy.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Very well. Agreed. My steward will call on you.

speaker: shivakiar
text: That is reasonable. D'accord.

speaker: shivakiar
text: That is a great deal, even for a ballroom.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Monsieur, you mistake me for an American heiress.

speaker: shivakiar
text: How amusing. Now tell me the real price.

speaker: shivakiar

text: Wonderful. Half of Cairo will want your name by Christmas.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Well, I have bought it. If anyone asks, it came from Istanbul.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Not today, monsieur. Au revoir.

speaker: shivakiar
text: I shall think about it. That usually means no.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Your cat sits on the carpet as if she owned it. I recognise the manner.

speaker: shivakiar
text: For the ballroom I want the finest thing in Egypt. A court carpet, silk, legendary. Find it, and I shall be very generous indeed.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Silk, from a court. Parfait. The ball will be remembered. Here, with my thanks.

speaker: shivakiar
text: I mentioned your stall at dinner. Expect a pasha or two. Be expensive.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Now that. That is a carpet for a princess.

speaker: shivakiar
text: That palace carpet you sold me. A cousin of mine knew the palace. There was never such a carpet. I laughed, but only afterwards.

text: The last carpet? The Belgian minister got down on his knees to look at it. I think it was the carpet.

speaker: shivakiar
text: How gallant.

speaker: shivakiar
text: She is very elegant. Keep her off my hem, please.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Mon Dieu. My kitchen maids would be ashamed of this.

speaker: shivakiar
text: At least you do not pretend it is fit for a ballroom. Take it away, please.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Well made, you say. So is a broom.

speaker: shivakiar
text: It is pretty. Half the villas in Zamalek have one just as pretty. I do not give ordinary balls.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Honest. Charming, even. Now show me what you keep for princes.

speaker: shivakiar
text: You make a fine case, monsieur. It remains a rich woman's rug, not a princess's.

speaker: shivakiar
text: You show a princess a carpet that needs washing? How very brave of you.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Well. You admit it. Have it made perfect, and then we may speak.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Beautiful underneath, you say. I am not in the habit of buying underneath.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Tell me, why should anyone at my ball care about this carpet? They have all seen Versailles.

speaker: shivakiar
text: You do not flatter me. How refreshing. Nobody in Cairo does that.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Very well. If it is as rare as you say, the French ambassador will be green. I like that.

speaker: shivakiar
text: A cousin of the old Ottoman house comes from Nice for the season. Since last year they have lost Istanbul. I want to give her something from a palace, so she feels at home again.
direction: A gift for a visiting royal cousin

speaker: shivakiar
text: My ball opens the season in December. Three hundred guests, the whole diplomatic corps, and a ballroom that must stop them at the door. I need the carpet they will talk about until spring.
direction: A centrepiece for her winter-season ball

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Good morning. I have half an hour. Let us use it well.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Peace be upon you. I am told your prices are honest. I will judge that myself.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Good morning again. Your last carpet has been walked on by half of Egypt. It holds.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I return. That is my verdict on your last sale.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: The reception hall at Bayt al-Umma. The door is open from morning until night.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: A hall full of people who have come a long way to speak. The floor should not be the loudest thing in it.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Sober colours. Good wool. Nothing that shouts.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Something Egyptian in spirit, or at least something that would not look foreign in an Egyptian house.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: You ask my budget before you show me anything. That is backwards. Show me first.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: For the hall, up to ninety pounds, if the carpet deserves it. For the study, less.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I decide. My wife will tell me afterwards whether I decided well.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I was a judge before I was anything else. A judge learns to hear the whole case before he speaks.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I have seen Malta and the Seychelles, and Gibraltar. I prefer Cairo.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Thank you. Tea, yes. Sugar, no.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: You present your evidence before you have heard the charge. Ask me what I need.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Yes. That is a serious carpet.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Good. Unroll it fully. I want to see the whole of it.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: It is adequate. I did not come for adequate.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Your last carpet has heard more poems than most critics.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: A generous gesture. There is a verse in that.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Look at her. Amber eyes, velvet paws. She is a better poem than most I have written.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: It is a carpet without a single line of verse in it. Honest, and silent.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: You admit it. Then let us find one that speaks.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Well made, you say. So is a wall.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: This is a peasant's song. Lovely in a field, lost in a salon.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Good. You hear the difference too.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Strong, yes. I did not come to buy strength.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Dust on the roses. A garden in need of rain.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Then wash it, and tell me the price of the rain.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Under the dust it blooms, you say. I hope you are right.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: You ask a price like a vizier. Tell me what I am buying, besides wool.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Plainly said. There is a kind of poetry in that too.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: The hands, the years, the dyes. Yes. Now it sounds like a poem.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: My salon looks onto the Nile. I want a carpet that continues the garden into the room, so that my guests walk from roses onto roses.
direction: A floral carpet for the salon at Karmet Ibn Hani

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: The room where I write. A lamp, a low table, and too many pages. I want a rug that gives me an image when I look down for a word.
direction: A rug for the room where he writes

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Good morning! Do not look so surprised. Even a star must buy carpets.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: They told me the best rugs at Giza are at this stall. Convince me they were right.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: I am back, and I am in a generous mood. Do not waste it.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Everyone asked about the last carpet. I told them your name. You are welcome.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: A stage, my dear. Twenty metres of boards, and every eye in Cairo on them.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: My salon, after the show. Candles, perfume, and people who think they are important.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Colour! Drama! Something that makes a room hold its breath.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: I want a carpet with an entrance, the way I have an entrance.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Money first? How unromantic. Show me something beautiful and I will forget to count.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: For the right carpet, three hundred pounds. For a miracle, three hundred and eighty. Not a pound more, and I mean it tonight.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: I decide. I have always decided. That is why there is a troupe with my name on it.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Every week another theatre opens on Emad el-Din. Let them. The audiences still know where to find me.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: They are putting in electric lamps everywhere now. Wonderful for the stage, cruel for the complexion.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Tea, yes. With mint, and not too sweet. I have to sing tonight.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: You bring out a rug before you know my stage? That is like handing me a costume before you know the part.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Oh! Now that is an entrance. Unroll it further, let me see it breathe.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Yes. Yes. The gallery would stand up for that.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: It is pleasant. Pleasant is for the chorus.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Hmm. It has good bones, but no voice.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: No, darling. That is for a clerk's parlour.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Take it away before somebody sees me looking at it.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Blue. Moonlight scenes only, and I do not play many of those.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Red. The colour of velvet curtains and applause. Wonderful.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: White? Under stage lamps it will look like a bedsheet.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Gold. Now you are speaking my language.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Dirty. I will not have dust on my hem.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Worn. It has had its season, I think.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Damaged. The audience sees everything, you know. Everything.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Oh, that is a story for the salon. Tell it again, slower, with feeling.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Marvellous. I will tell it better than you, of course, but it is marvellous.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: A nice little tale. It needs a second act.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: That many knots? Like rehearsals. Nobody sees them, but you see the result.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Knots are your business. Effect is mine.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Centre stage, under the lamps. I can see it already. So can the back row.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: In the salon, by the divan. They will talk about it until dawn.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: It would vanish under the lights, darling.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: It will last? Good. So will I.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: You said that already. Even I only repeat a chorus twice.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: From a palace! I will announce it from the stage.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

text: You see? Charm always works in the end.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: What a creature. She has the eyes of a prima donna.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Very pretty words. I say pretty words for a living. I know how they are made.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: It looks as if it has done three hundred matinees already. I do not buy tired things.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Good, you see it too. Then the price must remember it as well.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Yes, yes, the rarest in Cairo. Everyone says that to me. Occasionally it is true.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya

speaker: umm-kulthum

speaker: umm-kulthum

speaker: umm-kulthum

speaker: umm-kulthum

speaker: umm-kulthum

text: My teacher makes me understand every line of a poem before I may sing it. He is right, but it takes very long.

speaker: umm-kulthum

speaker: umm-kulthum

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Well. I have bought it. I shall find a story to excuse it.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Not today, I think. But I will remember the stall.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: No, thank you. The carpet and I have not been properly introduced.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Your cat approves. In my experience, cats are harsher critics than bishops.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Find me an old carpet with a real story, the kind a guest asks about before he sits down, and I shall pay a handsome bonus.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: There it is. Old, and talkative. Here is your bonus, with my thanks.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: I have mentioned your stall to a friend at the Residency. She is fussy. You will like her.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Good heavens. That belongs in a cathedral treasury.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: A dealer in the Old City laughed at the pasha story. I would rather you had simply said you did not know.

text: Your last carpet is doing splendidly. It has outlasted two committees already.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Gracious of you. I shall remember it.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: A very dignified animal. She would make an excellent district officer.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Handsome, but it was born about the same year as my motor car. I asked for something with a past.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Thank you for not pretending. Most men in this lane would swear it was woven for Saladin.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: A fine modern piece, yes. But I did not cross the Sinai for fine and modern.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: And where exactly was it before it came to you? I collect histories as much as carpets.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: An honest shrug. Rarer in a bazaar than a Ghiordes knot. I respect it.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: You make a fair case. I shall give it the benefit of the doubt, as one does with a charming guest.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Old is one thing. Threadbare is another. I cannot hang a sermon on bare warp.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Well said. Then let us price it as a scholar's rug, not a prince's.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: A good restorer, you say. I know a few in the Old City. Perhaps.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Tell me what this carpet will say when my guests sit down. If it says nothing, I do not want it.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Modest, and quite right. The best carpets let the guests do the talking.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Now that is a story I can tell at dinner. Go on.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: My study in Jerusalem is full of books, brass and people who stay too long. I want a carpet old enough to have opinions of its own.
direction: An antique carpet for the Governor's study

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: I owe a dinner to half of Cairo, and a present to one old friend in particular. Something bold, with a little swagger in it.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Peace be upon you. They told me in Cairo that the best carpets are found where you least expect them.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Good day. I have one hour before my next appointment, and I would like to spend it well.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Back again. The last carpet has been walked on by half of Jerusalem, and it still looks proud.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: I return. My guests ask where I found your carpet. I tell them nothing, naturally.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: A long reception hall, cushions along three walls, and a door that never stays closed.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: The hall where I receive guests. Coffee, conversation and a great many shoes.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: I want a carpet that makes a stranger straighten his tie.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Size, colour, dignity. In that order.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: You are quick to the purse. Thirty pounds, to begin.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: For a proper carpet, perhaps seventy pounds. A mayor must not look mean.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: The choice is mine. The bill, too.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: We are laying new water pipes in Jerusalem. Every street I fix, someone complains about the dust.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Cairo moves so quickly. In Jerusalem even the traffic stops to discuss things.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Tea, thank you. Without sugar. I have had enough sweetness from petitioners this week.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Already a carpet? You have not asked about my hall. A good merchant measures before he sells.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Yes. That one has standing. Open it fully.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Now that would greet a guest properly.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: It is respectable. Respectable is not enough.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Perhaps. Show me the border.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: No. That is for a clerk's front room.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: That would embarrass me before my own cousins.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

text: Very tasteful. Very quiet. My guests will think I have fallen on hard times.

text: With care, you say. My guests do not arrive with care. They arrive with news.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: I cannot receive a consul on a carpet that needs a bath.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Then the washing is on your account, and we talk.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

text: The municipality counts every pound, and so do I. Why is this worth what you ask?

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Knots and years and dyes. Good. You know your trade.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Every morning my hall fills with petitioners, merchants and cousins. The carpet is the first thing they see, and the first thing they judge.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi

speaker: sassoon-eskell

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: Peace be upon you. I have a little time and a clear budget. Both are precious.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: I return. Your last carpet has held its value better than the rupee.

speaker: sassoon-eskell

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: A library by the Tigris. Books, ledgers, a large table, and a floor that deserves better.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: A quiet room. I work there in the evenings, when the numbers behave.

speaker: sassoon-eskell

speaker: sassoon-eskell

speaker: sassoon-eskell

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: I decide. I have signed larger sums than this.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: A state budget is like a carpet. Every thread you pull on one side shows on the other.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: In Baghdad we speak Arabic in the market, Turkish in the old offices and English in the new ones. I keep accounts in all three.

direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: yusuf
voice_brief: Yusuf. Egyptian hotel owner, late 40s, brisk and practical, working-class Cairo accent, a little impatient, not unfriendly.

direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: yusuf

direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: yusuf
voice_brief: Yusuf. Egyptian hotel owner, late 40s, brisk and practical, working-class Cairo accent, a little impatient, not unfriendly.

direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: yusuf
voice_brief: Yusuf. Egyptian hotel owner, late 40s, brisk and practical, working-class Cairo accent, a little impatient, not unfriendly.
text: I had money in my pocket for once. A pity.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: yusuf
voice_brief: Yusuf. Egyptian hotel owner, late 40s, brisk and practical, working-class Cairo accent, a little impatient, not unfriendly.
text: I will write in my ledger: no purchase. It is a sad little line.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: yusuf
voice_brief: Yusuf. Egyptian hotel owner, late 40s, brisk and practical, working-class Cairo accent, a little impatient, not unfriendly.
text: Next time, my friend. The station trains wait for no one, and neither do I.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.

direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.

direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: I do not mean to be rude. Only, perhaps the hammam, when you have a moment?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: Your galabiya looks like Karim's old one. I patched that one twice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: You look tired. Have you eaten today?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: I would offer to mend that sleeve, but my mother would say it is not proper.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: Oh. There is nothing quite right today. That is all right.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: I think these are a little too plain even for our little flat. Maybe next time.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: I had so hoped to surprise Karim. Never mind.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: I will come back, I promise. God keep you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mariam
voice_brief: Mariam. Young Egyptian woman, about 22, soft and warm, shy, hesitant pauses, gentle Shubra accent.
text: Do not worry. Something lovely will come in, I am sure of it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Ya salaam! You smell like the back room of my coffee house on a Friday.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Brother, even my backgammon players go to the hammam once a week.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Stand there, not here. The wind is from your side.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: That galabiya! Did you win it at backgammon, or lose it?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: You look like my customers. That is not a compliment, but it is not an insult either.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Dusty, eh? Never mind. Dust is free, and so is my advice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Nothing today that would survive forty men and their coffee.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Hmm. I came with coins in my pocket, and they are going home with me.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Not today, brother. Not today.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: Come for coffee, and bring me better rugs. In that order.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hassan
voice_brief: Egyptian coffee-house owner, mid fifties, warm, jolly, loud laugh, talks with his hands
text: I will tell everyone you are a good man. I will not mention the rugs.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh dear. I say this as a friend. Soap is really quite inexpensive.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I shall breathe through my handkerchief, if you don't mind. It's the heat, I expect.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Goodness. I shall have to leave that out of my letter home. Mother would faint.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: The pasha's coachman dresses better, and he is not trying to sell me anything.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Rather dusty, aren't we? Never mind. So is Cairo.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: In Surrey one would at least brush one's coat before opening the shop.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Oh. I'm afraid these look rather like the mats outside the vicarage.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: I did so want something to write home about. There is nothing to write home about.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Forgive me, but the children would wear through these by Easter.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Well, I shall say you were very charming, and leave it at that.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: whitcombe
voice_brief: English governess, mid thirties, Surrey accent, precise, polite, dry humour
text: Good afternoon. Do try a little harder, won't you?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: You smell like my camels. My camels, at least, have the excuse of the desert.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: In Sinai we have no water and we wash. You have the Nile.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: Ha. Stand downwind, my friend, like a good camel.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: Your clothes are like mine after the crossing. But I have crossed the Canal. You have crossed nothing.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: Dust does not frighten me. I was born in it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: A poor coat on an honest man is no shame. We will see if you are honest.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: Nothing here I would put before a guest in my tent. A pity.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: These would not last one night of wind. I am sorry, but it is true.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: I sold good camels to buy a good rug. There is no good rug.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: I go back to Imbaba. The camel traders lie, but at least they have camels.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: salem
text: Peace be upon you. Find better wool, and I will find you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Speaking as a physician, you are overdue for a bath. By some days.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I would prescribe hot water, soap and a good scrubbing. The fee is waived.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: My patients sit closer to me than this, and they are ill. You have no excuse.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I came here with nothing once. I still brushed my coat every morning.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: The dust is general. The frayed cuff is a choice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: My consulting room sees pashas. They would not let you past the porter.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: These are honest, but they are not fine. My patients notice fine.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: In Aintab the village looms made better than this. I remember them.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Is there nothing with a proper knot count? No? I see.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: Good day. My diagnosis is poor stock. The cure is patience.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: kasparian
voice_brief: Armenian physician, fifties, soft-spoken, exact, a little weary
text: I will come again when you have something worthy of the consulting room.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: Monsieur, you smell like a camel that has read about soap but never tried it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: I have no time, and now I have no air either.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: Please. Even the bales in our basement smell better, and they came from Basra.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: Our porters dress better. And we pay our porters very badly.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: Is this a costume? Are you playing the poor merchant for the tourists?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: You look like a rug nobody bought. How fitting.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: Is this a carpet shop or the bargain table at a jumble sale?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: My customers have left the village. They do not wish to buy it back.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: I cannot sell this on Rue Chérif Pacha. I could not give it away on Rue Chérif Pacha.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: I write your name in my notebook. Under the heading: do not return.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: levy
text: Merci, no. I have a train, and you have a great deal of work to do.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: My son, cleanliness is a kind of prayer. You have missed a few.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: Forgive an old man. The hammam would do you good, body and soul.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: Even the monks in the desert wash, now and then. Now would be a good time.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: A plain robe is no sin. I have worn this cassock for twenty years.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: You look like you have been sweeping the church. That is honest work.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: Never mind the dust, my son. We are all dust in the end.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: These are humble, my son. But the church deserves a little more than humble.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: The committee gave me money for a good rug. I cannot bring them a mat.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: Nothing quite fit for the altar today. Perhaps God will send you something.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: God keep you. And your stock. Especially your stock.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: antonios
text: I will pray for you, my son. And for better carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My God. Did something die in that galabiya, or are you merely resting?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: I have smelled better at the cotton exchange in August, and they sweat for money.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Stand back, my friend. My tailor will charge me to air this suit.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My servants dress better than you, and they complain about their wages.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: You look like a man who lost everything in the cotton crash. Did you?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Please tell me you have a better galabiya at home. Please.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Is this a carpet shop or a doormat museum?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: My servants walk on rugs like this. My dogs walk on rugs like this.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Salvago would laugh. Salvago has a villa full of real carpets. Show me real carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: I go to the races. At least there the horses are groomed.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: benakis
voice_brief: Greek cotton broker from Alexandria, forties, charming, expansive, vain
text: Call me when you have something from a pasha's house, not his stable.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: Let the record show the merchant has not bathed. The evidence is overwhelming.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: I have cross-examined sweatier men, but they were in the dock.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: Your case is not helped by the smell, my friend. No judge would sit this close.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: You dress like a defendant who could not afford counsel.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: In Paris they would call this rustic. In Qasr el-Nil we call it shabby.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: Dust on a galabiya is circumstantial. Dust on everything is conclusive.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: Is this the stock, or the evidence against you?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: I have seen better rugs in the clerks' room at the Mixed Courts.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: My study is lined with law books. These would embarrass the law books.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: Case dismissed. For lack of merit.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: wasif
text: I rest my case. Somewhere with a better class of carpet.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: Ah. One notices things, monsieur. One notices this rather strongly.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: At the legation we would call this an incident. I shall be discreet.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: I have negotiated with men in the Hauran who bathed more recently.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: A most informal costume. Very authentic. Very dusty.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: The High Commission has a dress code. You would fail it at the gate.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: One need not wear a frock coat. But one could perhaps wear a clean one.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: Charming. For a consulate in a very small town.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: I am furnishing a residence, monsieur, not a guardhouse.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: Show me something that has hung in a palace. These have lain in a courtyard.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: I shall say nothing of this in my report. Nothing at all.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: martel
text: Au revoir. When you find something worthy of Beirut, send word to the legation.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: In Isfahan a merchant bathes before he unrolls a carpet. It is only respect.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: Brother, you smell like a wool bale after the monsoon.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: I crossed the desert in a Nairn car and I smell better than you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: A merchant who dresses like this is either very poor or very clever. I think poor.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: In Baghdad we say, sell the robe before you sell the rug.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: Dust on the merchant, dust on the rugs. Paris does not buy dust.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: These? In Baghdad I use these to wrap the good ones.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: I sell to Paris, my friend. Paris does not buy village mats.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: Show me a Kashan, a Tabriz, something from a royal loom. This is from somebody's goat.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: I will buy from the Armenian in the Khan. He at least lies about better rugs.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rustam
text: Peace be upon you, brother. And upon your poor stock.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: Say, friend, have you been sleeping in the stable with the camels?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: Back home in Ohio we have a thing called a bathtub. You'd love it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: Whew. Shepheard's would not let you past the terrace. Not even for tea.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: You look like a fellow who sold his best clothes to buy his worst rugs.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: Is that galabiya an antique? Because I don't collect those.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: I've seen railway tramps better turned out than this. And I've met a few.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: I have seen finer rugs under the feet of mules at Jaffa Gate.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: I came for a museum piece. These are for wiping boots on.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: Friend, I buy what palaces are ashamed to part with. Not what villages are glad to be rid of.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: I'll be at Shepheard's. Come find me when you have something worth the walk.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: hollister
text: So long. Don't take it personal. Actually, take it a little personal.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Good heavens. Has somebody opened a drain, or is it only you?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: You smell like the servants' quarters on a hot night. I have never been there, and now I need not go.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Please do not come any closer. My perfume came from Paris and it is losing.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: My footmen would be dismissed for looking like that. Twice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: How very picturesque. Like a beggar in an Orientalist painting.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Did you dress in the dark, or simply in the dust?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: My dear, my maid's maid would not wipe her slippers on these.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Mon Dieu. My kitchen maids would be ashamed of these.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Come back when you have something from a palace, not a village.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: I shan't be sending you an invitation this season. Or any season.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: shivakiar
text: Do not trouble to bow. It would only stir up the smell.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

text: You come before your king unwashed? That is either very brave or very foolish.
