text: The chamberlain will air this room when you are gone. For some days.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: A merchant at Abdeen should smell of rosewater, not of the road.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: My palace guards are better dressed, and they stand in the sun all day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: You come to Abdeen in a galabiya fit for the field. Remarkable.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: In Italy they taught me that a man is known by his linen. What should I know of you?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: This is a village piece. You have brought village pieces to Abdeen.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: I founded a university, merchant. I know a doormat when I see one.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: Come back with a carpet from a palace loom, or do not come back.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: The audience is ended. The chamberlain will show you out, quickly.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fuad
voice_brief: King Fuad I of Egypt, late 50s. Formal, precise and reserved; educated in Italy, a faint Italian colouring to his English. Never hurried.
text: We shall not speak of this again. And neither, I think, will you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: Oh! Somebody bring the eau de cologne. Quickly.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: The sea air at Ras el-Tin is so fresh. You have undone it in a moment.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: In Paris the merchants smell of lavender. Here, apparently, of camel.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: Is this what they wear in the bazaar now? I shall not tell Vogue.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: My ladies-in-waiting are staring. I cannot blame them.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: Such a sad little galabiya. Did it come with the rugs?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: These would not do for my maid's bedroom, let alone mine.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: In Paris they would call this charming. In Cairo we call it firewood.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: I read the Paris magazines, darling. Nothing in them looks like this.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: Adieu. Do find something beautiful. I am told it exists.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: nazli
voice_brief: Queen Nazli of Egypt, early 30s. Warm, elegant and a little amused; Alexandrian French in her vowels.
text: I shall go and look at the sea. It, at least, is not shabby.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: In the tent we smell of smoke and horses. You smell of neither. Worse.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: A poet would find a verse for this smell. I am a poet, and I will not.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: My guards have asked to wait outside. I do not blame them.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: I prefer the tent to the palace. But even in the tent, one brushes one's robe.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: A poor robe does not trouble me. A careless one does.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: You look like a man who lost a chess game and his coat with it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: I am building a palace, merchant. You show me what goes under a goat.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: In chess one does not open with a pawn and call it a queen.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: Bring me a carpet worthy of my father's house in Mecca. These are worthy of a stable.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: Checkmate, merchant. You never had the pieces.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: abdullah
voice_brief: Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, early 40s. Hospitable, humorous and poetic; a Hejazi Arab speaking English slowly and with pleasure.
text: I return to Amman. The wind there is cleaner, and so are the carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: I have ridden with Bedouin through the whole war. None smelled quite like this.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: Forgive me. A king learns to be polite. But not this polite.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: In Damascus the merchants bathed before the Friday market. It was a good custom.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: I have seen fine things in Istanbul, in Damascus, in London. This is not one of them.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: The court in Baghdad has patience. But it also has a dress code.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: A merchant should look like his best carpet. I hope your best carpet looks better.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: I lived in Istanbul, merchant. I have seen what a real palace carpet is.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: These are fine for a guardroom. I did not come to furnish a guardroom.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: Come back when you have something from the old courts, not the old market.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: I am a patient man. Not, it seems, patient enough.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: faisal
voice_brief: King Faisal I of Iraq, early 40s. Soft-spoken, courteous and careful; a diplomat weighing each word.
text: Peace be upon you. May your next caravan carry better wool.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: The Republic has abolished many old customs. Bathing was not one of them.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: A modern nation begins with a clean man. Start with yourself.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: I have smelled the trenches at Gallipoli. You are a close second.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: We have banned the fez. Do not tempt me to ban that galabiya.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: A man in a clean collar can build a country. A man in that can barely sell a rug.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: Dress for the century you live in, merchant. It is 1925.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: I want good Anatolian work, not the sweepings of a sleepy village.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: The Republic has abolished the old ways, and it seems you have abolished the good carpets. Answer quickly, I have a country to run.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: Bring me the finest loom in Anatolia. Not the tiredest.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: Forward, merchant. That way. Out.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ataturk
voice_brief: Mustafa Kemal Pasha, 44. Brisk, direct and decisive; short sentences, a Turkish accent, no small talk.
text: Çankaya deserves better. Frankly, so do your customers.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: You will forgive a plain remark. The hammam is not expensive.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I have stood in crowded halls all year. This is worse.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: A merchant should smell of wool and cedar, not of the road.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Your galabiya has seen hard service. So, it seems, have you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I do not ask for elegance. I ask for a clean collar.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: You look like a man who slept at the stall. Perhaps you did.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Nothing here fit for Bayt al-Umma. I am sorry to say it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: These are honest pieces for honest rooms. Not for mine.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I expected more. I will not pretend otherwise.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: Send word when you have something serious. Good day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: saad-zaghloul
text: I will come back when your stock deserves the visit.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: Forgive me. Perhaps a little rosewater, before the next customer?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: I will stand in the breeze, if you do not mind. It is a warm day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: My mother always said a clean merchant sells twice as fast. She was usually right.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: Your sleeve is torn. Someone at home should mend it for you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: You look tired. Have you eaten today?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: A little care in dress is a courtesy to your customers. I say it kindly.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: There is nothing quite right for the salon today. Never mind.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: These are good honest carpets, but not for a room where guests are received.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: I had hoped for something finer. Perhaps another week.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: Do send word when something special comes in. I mean that.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: safiya-zaghloul
text: Good morning. I am sure next time will be better.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: I will be frank. You need a bath before you need a customer.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: I am standing upwind on purpose. I hope you understand.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: A clean stall and a clean merchant. It is not too much to ask.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: You dress as though you expect nobody to look at you. People do look.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: A torn galabiya does not inspire confidence in the carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: If you respect your stock, you might extend the courtesy to yourself.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: There is nothing here of the quality I need. I am sorry.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: Coarse work, all of it. Our weavers can do far better.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: I came for fine workmanship. I do not see any today.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: Improve your stock and I will come back. That is a promise, not a threat.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: huda-shaarawi
text: Good morning. I hope to find more next time.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: I rely on my nose more than most men. Today it is not happy with you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: Forgive me. The hammam, perhaps, before the next customer?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: I can smell the road on you from here. Several days of it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: Your sleeve brushed my hand. It is frayed through. You should see to that.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: My companion tells me your galabiya has seen better years. He is too polite to say more.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: I cannot see your clothes. My companion can, and he is wincing.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: Everything under my hand today feels coarse. I am sorry.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: Nothing here I could walk on for years. Nothing with a known history.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: I came hoping for something quiet and true. Not today, it seems.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: I will return when your stock has improved. I have a patient memory.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: taha-hussein
text: Good morning. Better luck to both of us next time.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: My friend, a rose would faint here. Perhaps the hammam, and then the carpets?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: I came for the scent of wool and found the scent of the road.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: The breeze from the river is kind. It is working very hard for you today.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Your galabiya is an elegy. A long, sad one.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: A merchant of beautiful things should look a little less like a ruin.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: You look like a verse that has been crossed out twice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Not one carpet here that sings. Only carpets that mutter.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: This is prose, my friend, all of it. I came for poetry.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: The garden I was looking for is not in your stall today.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: I will come back when your stock has found its voice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ahmed-shawqi
text: Good day. May your next caravan bring you roses.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Darling, my dressing room smells of roses. Your stall smells of something else.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: I will stand over here, by the jasmine. It is not personal.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Even my stagehands visit the hammam before a first night.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: That galabiya would not pass as a costume for a beggar in the third act.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: A merchant should dress for his audience. Your audience today is me.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: I do not mind humble. I mind careless.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Nothing here would survive the footlights. What a pity.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: These are for a provincial touring company, darling, not for me.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: I came for a sensation and found a rehearsal.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: The curtain comes down on this visit. No applause, I am afraid.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: munira-al-mahdiyya
text: Call me when you have something worthy of a star.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: Forgive me. Perhaps a wash before customers come.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: I will stand in the doorway, if you do not mind. For the air.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: My mother says cleanliness is half of faith. I agree with her.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: Your galabiya is torn at the sleeve. My mother would mend it for you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: You look tired. A merchant should rest, too.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: I do not mind plain clothes. But clean clothes are respect for the customer.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: I do not see anything fine enough today. I am sorry.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: These are honest rugs, but not careful ones.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: Perhaps next time. I will be patient.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: Thank you. Peace be upon you. Perhaps another day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: umm-kulthum
text: I will look elsewhere today. Do not be offended.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: My friend, there is eau de Cologne in every chemist on Fuad Street.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: Forgive me, I will stand upwind. My suit is new.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: A little soap, a little Cologne. It is 1925, after all.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: That galabiya belongs to the last century. So, I fear, does the stall.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: Presentation is half of any art. Even carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: I would lend you my tailor, but he is very expensive.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: Everything here is so old-fashioned. I hoped for something new.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: These are my grandfather's carpets. I love him, but no.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: Nothing modern at all. What a disappointment.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: Not today. Perhaps when you have something of this century.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: mohamed-abdel-wahab
text: I must go. Good day, and good luck.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: Forgive me, but I have a sensitive nose as well as a sensitive ear.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: I will stand a little further off. The violin case too.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: A visit to the hammam, perhaps. It tunes the body.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: A musician on stage is always well dressed. A merchant in his stall, too.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: That sleeve is fraying like an old bow.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: Presentation, my friend. It is half of the performance.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: I heard nothing in tune today. A pity.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: These are fine for a café, not for a music room.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: Nothing fine enough, I am afraid. Nothing at all.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: I will take my leave. Perhaps next season.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sami-al-shawwa
text: Good day. I must go and tune.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: My son, the hammam is a pleasant place. You should visit it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: I will sit by the door, if I may. For the air.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: Forgive an old man for saying so. A wash would help business.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: Your galabiya is tired, my son. So are you, I think.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: A tidy stall and a tidy merchant. My father always said so.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: That sleeve needs a needle. I would lend you mine, but I only mend songs.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: Nothing here sings to me today. I am sorry.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: These are good for a café. I need something for a salon.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: Not one flower in the whole stall. What a pity.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: Another day, my son. Peace be upon you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: daoud-hosni
text: I will go. Perhaps next week you will have a garden.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: My friend, even the backstage at the end of a summer run smells sweeter than this.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: I will stand stage left, if you do not mind. Upwind.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: A merchant should enter like a leading man, not like the stable boy in the third act.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: Costume matters. You are dressed for a very small part.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: That galabiya has had a longer run than any play I have staged.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: Presentation, my friend. The audience judges the actor before he speaks.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: Nothing here could hold a stage. These are extras, not stars.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: I came to cast a leading carpet. I see only the chorus.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: Timid pieces, all of them. My foyer would swallow them whole.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: Call me when you have a star. Until then, the house is dark.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: youssef-wahbi
text: Good day. Rehearse your stock, and try again next season.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Oh. Perhaps a little rosewater, my dear? Just a suggestion.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Forgive me, I will stand by the door. The air is nicer there.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: In the theatre we say the audience can smell fear. I think they could smell this too.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: You have such good carpets and such a sad galabiya.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: A little starch in the collar would do wonders for you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Dress for the part, my dear. Even a merchant has a part.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Nothing pretty today. That makes me a little sad.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: These are all so heavy. I wanted something that floats.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Not one of them would look nice in a photograph.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Send me a note when something lovely arrives.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: aziza-amir
text: Goodbye for now. Next time, bring me romance.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: Darling, the hammam is cheaper than your worst rug. Consider it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: I have shared dressing rooms with twelve actresses in August. This is worse.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: I will keep my cigarette lit, I think. For both our sakes.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: If my cartoonists saw you, you would be on the back page.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: You look like a critic after a bad opening night.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: A clean shirt is the cheapest advertisement there is.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: Nothing here worth a single line. Not even a caption.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: Everything well behaved and nothing interesting. A pity.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: I came for a conversation piece. I found a silence.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: Send word when you have something with opinions.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rose-al-youssef
text: Good day. I will not write about this visit, which is a kindness.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: Oh! Oh, forgive me, it is only the smell. Is something wrong with the drains?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: My mother would send you straight to the hammam, and give you soap.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: I will hold my shawl to my nose, I hope you do not mind.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: Your poor sleeve! Does nobody mend for you?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: You look so tired. Do you sleep at all?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: Such beautiful rugs, and such a sorry galabiya.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: Oh, nothing here makes my heart jump today.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: They are all so grey and sad. Where is the red?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: I wanted to fall in love, and nothing is even trying.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: Next time, please have something warm for me. I will come back.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: fatma-rushdi
text: Goodbye. Do not be sad; I am always coming back.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: Forgive my frankness, but hygiene is the first principle of good business.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: I will stand in the doorway, if you permit. The air is better there.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: A client notices everything. That includes the air in the shop.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: Presentation is part of the product. Your clothes are underselling your stock.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: In Beirut I would not let a salesman meet a client like that.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: A pressed collar costs little and returns a great deal.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: Nothing here of the quality I need. The weave is loose throughout.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: Decent market pieces. Not one of them for a serious room.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: I had hoped for precision. I see approximation.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: Please write to me in Beirut when something fine comes in.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: charles-corm
text: Good day. I will try again on my next visit to Cairo.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: I have smelled the Jerusalem tanneries in August. You are running them close.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Forgive me if I admire the carpets from slightly upwind.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: There is a hammam behind the Khan. I recommend it, as a friend.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: That galabiya has a history, I see. Rather more than some of your carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: A merchant should be at least as well kept as his stock.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Tired clothes make a customer wonder about tired prices.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Four rugs. I have seen fuller stalls at a church jumble sale.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: A very select collection. Selected, I suspect, by misfortune.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Is this all? I had hoped for a treasure cave, and found a cupboard.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: I shall look elsewhere, I think. Do write when the stall has grown up.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: ronald-storrs
text: Not enough to choose from. Good day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: My friend, a wash would help your sales more than any carpet.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: I will stand here, by the air. Forgive me.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: In Jerusalem a merchant bathes before the market. It is good business.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Your clothes are tired. It makes the carpets look tired too.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: A man selling to a mayor should look the part.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Dust on the merchant, dust on the goods. My guests would notice.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: So few carpets. Is the rest in storage, or in your imagination?
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: I came for a choice, not a single option.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: A small stall for such a large city.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: There is nothing here for my hall. Good day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: raghib-nashashibi
text: Come back to me when your stall is worthy of a reception room.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: The air here is costing you customers. I can put a figure on it.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: A bath costs almost nothing. The sales you lose cost rather more.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: I will stand a little further back. It improves my concentration.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: A shabby merchant invites a lower offer. I will make one.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: Your clothes are depreciating faster than your stock.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: Presentation is part of the price. You are discounting yourself.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: This inventory would not fill a single line of my ledger.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: Too little choice. Too little competition among your own carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: A portfolio of four is not a portfolio. It is a risk.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: Insufficient stock. I shall come back when the figures improve.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: sassoon-eskell
text: Nothing here meets the requirement. Good day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: Forgive me, my friend. Soap is cheap, and so is water.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: I tell my pupils to wash before class. I would say the same to you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: I will sit on this side, if you do not mind. The breeze is kinder.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: A tired galabiya. I have one like it, but I do not wear it to work.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: Look after yourself, and the customers will look after you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: You look as though you have not slept. A rug seller must be rested to bargain.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: Only a few rugs. Like a library with one shelf.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: It is a small stall. But small is not always bad. Sometimes it is only small.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: Not much to choose from. I had hoped to browse.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: There is nothing for me today. Perhaps next time.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: khalil-sakakini
text: I will come back when you have more pages to turn.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: I have shared tents with camels that were fresher. Forgive my candour.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: A bath, I think, before the next customer.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: I will stand upwind. It is nothing personal. It is purely practical.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: You look as though you have crossed the Nafud on foot.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: A merchant who looks neglected makes me wonder about his carpets.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: Your clothes have seen better days. So, I suspect, have you.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: Is that everything? I have catalogued fuller trenches.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: Hardly a selection. More an accident.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: Four rugs. I expected more of Giza.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: Nothing here for me. Good day.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: gertrude-bell
text: Come back to me when you have something worth looking at.
direction: Reacting to the merchant's appearance or stock.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Ah, the man with the cat. Come, sit. I have things you cannot afford and a few you can.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Look who crawled in from Giza. Sit down before you fall down.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Welcome, welcome, pasha of the three rugs. Tea first. Then I rob you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You again? Good. A merchant who comes back is a merchant who is selling. Or begging.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Come in, nephew. Mind the doorstep. It is worth more than your stall.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Ahlan! I heard you coming from Bab Zuweila. Nobody else walks like a lost goat.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Sit. Drink. Say nothing clever. My heart is old.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: The tram stopped outside and I prayed it was a rich Englishman. It was you. God is testing me.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You drive a hard bargain for a man with three rugs. Fine. Take it and go before I wake up.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Fine! For your father. He will laugh at me over backgammon tonight, I know it.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You haggle like a Khan el-Khalili grandmother. I am proud and I am ruined.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Take it. My children will eat bread and onions tonight, and it is your fault.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Where did you learn that? Not from me. I would never teach you to rob me.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Fine, fine. Write it down, the day Rashid lost. Nobody will believe you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You win. Now stop smiling, it does not suit you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Enough! You have squeezed me like Egyptian cotton. Take the rug.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: No. That price is the price. Ask again and I charge you for the tea.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You insult me. You insult my shop. You insult my grandfather, God rest him.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: That offer? I would not take that from a pasha, and you are no pasha.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Habibi, even the Wafd could not negotiate that price down. Try again tomorrow.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Ha! You offer me that with a straight face? Your father had better jokes.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Cotton prices are falling, the pound is falling, and so is my patience. No.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: No. Go sell your cat if you are short.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I have heard better offers from the donkeys outside. And they cannot talk.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Good choice. Sell it well and come back.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: It is yours. Treat it better than you treat your galabiya.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Sold! Now carry it carefully. That rug has seen more of Egypt than you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: A fine rug. Too fine for your stall, but who am I to judge. I am only right.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Take it, take it. And do not let the cat sleep on it for a week.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Good. Sell it for double, and tell nobody where you got it so cheap.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Mabrouk. You have bought something that will not embarrass you. For once.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Go on, show it to the Englishwomen. They will pay anything if you say it is old.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I will write it in the book. Five days. Do not make me come to Giza. I hate Giza.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Credit, he says. Fine. My book is heavier than the Pharaoh's coffin, one more line will not hurt.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I write your name in the book next to the pasha who ran off to Paris. Do not join him.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: On credit. God help me, I am soft like fresh bread.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Take it. Pay me on time and I will stop shouting. A little.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Written down. The ink is permanent, nephew, and so is my memory.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Credit? You have not earned credit yet. You have barely earned a chair.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: No credit. Even the Bank Misr would laugh you out the door.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Credit for you? My book says no, my heart says no, and my wife says absolutely not.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: This one came in this morning. It will not be here tomorrow.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Look at this. No, look with your eyes, not your empty pockets.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: A rug like this comes once a year. Like my wife's good mood.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: This belonged to a pasha who backed the wrong side. His loss, my profit, your chance.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Careful. Touch it gently. It is older than the Wafd and prettier than both of us.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Half the museums in London want this. I am giving it to you. Because I am a fool.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Do not breathe on it. I mean that kindly, but do not.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Needs work, but under the dirt is a good rug. Cheap, because I am lazy.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: It has a hole. So does your roof, and you still live there.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: A little torn. A little faded. Like me. But good bones.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Moths had a feast on this one. Clean it, mend it, and sell it as antique.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Damaged, yes. But so is your reputation, and I still sell to you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Wash it once and it will shine. Unlike your shoes.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: The camel sat on it. The camel was very comfortable. Now it is yours.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Your stall is so small the flies queue outside.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Did you hear? Another Englishman fainted in Tutankhamun's tomb. I think he saw the price of your rugs.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You know the pasha across the street? He owes me more than you. It makes me love you a little.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: The trams go faster every year. And still you arrive late.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: They say cotton is down again. Good. Now the cotton men haggle like you. Badly.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Everybody in the Khan asks me about you. I tell them you are my nephew. Then I apologise.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: The Wafd wants independence. I want my money. We are both still waiting.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: My tea boy sells more than you, and he only sells tea.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You call that a stall? I have seen bigger stalls on a donkey cart.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Lord Carnarvon died of a curse. You will die of haggling. It is slower.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Tell me honestly, do you sell rugs, or do you just sit on them?

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: An Englishwoman asked me today if the pyramids were for sale. I sent her to you. You owe me.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I have known you since you were this tall. You were cleverer then.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Ya salaam, what is that smell? Did the cat die in your pocket?

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Stand over there. No, further. By the window. Outside the window is also fine.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Nephew, the hammam is open every day. It is not only for pashas.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You smell like a camel that lost an argument with a goat.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: My customers left. They said a sewer walked in. I said no, only my nephew.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I will give you a discount if you promise to wash before you come back.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Did you sleep in the Nile? The fish would be offended.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Soap costs two piastres. I will lend it to you. On credit.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Wash, habibi. Buyers use their noses before they use their purses.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Even the flies are keeping away from you, and flies have no standards.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Still in that galabiya? You have money now. Buy a shirt, it will not bite you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You dress like a beggar and you have pounds in your pocket. The buyers see the galabiya, not the pounds.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: That galabiya has more holes than a fisherman's net.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: A merchant with money should look like a merchant with money. You look like the man who sweeps for one.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Your father wore a good coat even when he was poor. You are rich and you wear a sack.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Buy a coat, nephew. The pashas will not buy from a man they would tip.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I have seen potato sacks with better tailoring.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Are you saving for a coat, or saving the galabiya for the museum?

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: The Englishman at Shepheard's asked if you were my servant. I said yes. You deserved it.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Look at you! A real merchant. For a moment I thought a pasha had come to pay his debts.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: A fine coat. Finally. Now if only the man inside matched it.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Very elegant. The coat is worth more than your stall. Try not to spill tea on it.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Oh, the gentleman has arrived. Shall I stand up? No. My knees say no.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Good cloth. You look like somebody. I cannot remember who, but somebody.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Now the rich ladies will listen to you. Until you open your mouth.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You look so good I will raise my prices.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Your father would smile to see you in that. Then he would ask how much it cost, and faint.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Beautiful. Now walk slowly. Rich men never hurry.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Your purse is so light the wind could steal it.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Empty pockets again? Here, have tea. Tea is free. Everything else, no.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I can hear your purse. It is crying.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You have less money than a beggar at Sayyida Zeinab, and he has a better spot.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: No money? Sell something. Sell the cat. No, do not sell the cat. Sell something.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Look at me, nephew. Everyone starts poor. Not everyone stays poor. Go sell.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: With that money you can buy one thread. Choose carefully.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Even the pigeons outside have more savings than you.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Do not worry. Your father was broke twice. Both times he came back. You will too.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I would lend you money, but my book already has your name in capitals.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: So much money! Who did you rob? Tell me, I want a share.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Look at those coins. Suddenly I remember how much I love my nephew.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Rich, are we? Then today my prices are also rich.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: You have money now. Be careful. Money brings cousins you never knew you had.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Who is this big man with the heavy purse? Is King Fuad visiting?

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Your pockets are full and my shelves are full. God has made us for each other.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Rich already? Your father took twenty years. You are either clever or a thief.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: With that purse you could buy a tram. Buy rugs instead. From me.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Money suits you. It makes you walk straighter and smell almost acceptable.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Do not tell the tax man. And do not tell my wife, she will want a new dress.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: How is Saffron? Better fed than you, I hope. That cat has taste.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Your cat sleeps on the best rug in your stall. She is the only one there who knows quality.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Saffron is the brains of your business. You are only the hands.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: Bring Saffron next time. She haggles better than you and she only says meow.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: That cat has more dignity than half the pashas in Cairo.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: I once offered your father five pounds for that cat. He said no. Smart man.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
text: If Saffron ever leaves you, send her to me. I have a cushion ready.

speaker: rashid
voice_brief: Uncle Rashid. Old Cairo merchant, sixties, gruff, teasing, secretly fond, fast talker.
